unit_fields_label: Estimated units in 1-, 2-, 3-4 and 5+ unit buildings (Building Permits Survey)

data_release.release_date_basis: Last-Modified date of the state annual file

forecast_gap_text: 2026 has no full-year permit count by the cutoff; the baseline carries the 2025 rule level through it.
rule_text: state mean of 2021-2025 permits x the county's share of state permits in 2016-2025
formula: state component = 5 x mean of 2021-2025 state units = 5 x (47,894 + 28,149 + 25,320 + 24,810 + 25,709) / 5 = 151,882 units (rule top_down_share, state series only; county shares do not change the sum)

baseline_pa_window_2022_2025.label: Pennsylvania baseline window sensitivity: 2022-2025 mean instead of the shipped window
baseline_pa_window_2022_2025.formula: 5 x (28,149 + 25,320 + 24,810 + 25,709) / 4 = 5 x 25,997 = 129,985 units; difference from the shipped state component 151,882 = -21,897 units (-14.4%)
baseline_pa_window_2022_2025.status: Disclosed historical-window sensitivity. Named after the spike was seen, so not pre-registered. Not a replacement baseline; never subtracted from any reform or package result.
baseline_pa_window_2022_2025.rationale: Pennsylvania's 2021 total is far above 2022-2025, and the shipped rule's five-year window includes it. Showing the four-year mean makes the effect of that one model choice visible. Named after the spike was seen, so it is a disclosed sensitivity, not a pre-registered test or a replacement baseline.

bridge.method_text: Carry annual through the gap: the rule's yearly level from the last full year of data is used unchanged for the gap year and each projected year. The gap year is not projected separately and adds nothing to the five-year total.

nowcast.label: 2026 nowcast from monthly year-to-date permits (diagnostic only)
caveats: A year-to-date count is never treated as a full year.
Monthly and annual files differ in reporting and imputation; the share s absorbs that difference as well as the season.
Release dates are the files' Last-Modified dates on the Census server; a re-posted file shows a later date than its first release.
The history files are as posted now; earlier copies were not archived, so this is a revised-data exercise.

state.formula: nowcast = YTD 2026 Jan-Sep / s; YTD = 19,096; s = YTD(y, Jan-Sep) / annual(y) for y in 2021-2025 (2021 0.595, 2022 0.656, 2023 0.707, 2024 0.737, 2025 0.757); low / middle / high use s = 0.757 / 0.707 / 0.595 = 25,228 / 26,998 / 32,110 units; the carried annual level is 30,376 units (the shipped rule's state level, mean of 2021-2025). Diagnostic only: no estimate uses it.
state.carried_annual_basis: the shipped rule's state level, mean of 2021-2025

rows.label: Historical years used
rows.text: level from 2021–2025 permits; county shares from 2016–2025; rules tested on 1990–2025. Rule: state mean of 2021-2025 permits x the county's share of state permits in 2016-2025.

rows.label: Permit columns counted
rows.text: Estimated units in 1-, 2-, 3-4 and 5+ unit buildings (Building Permits Survey) (est_1_units, est_2_units, est_3-4_units, est_5+_units). The reported-only columns are not used.

rows.label: Data release
rows.text: 2025 annual files (final), posted 2026-05-14 (Last-Modified date of the state annual file).

rows.label: Information cutoff
rows.text: 2026-11-24: nothing released after this date is used (as_of in assumptions/outcome.yaml).

rows.label: Projected years and gap
rows.text: 2027–2031; gap year 2026. 2026 has no full-year permit count by the cutoff; the baseline carries the 2025 rule level through it. Carry annual through the gap: the rule's yearly level from the last full year of data is used unchanged for the gap year and each projected year. The gap year is not projected separately and adds nothing to the five-year total.

rows.label: 2026 nowcast (diagnostic only)
rows.text: 25,228 to 32,110 homes, middle 26,998, from 19,096 permits in January–September (file st2609y.txt, posted 2026-10-27); the baseline carries 30,376 a year through the gap. No estimate uses the nowcast.
rows.formula: nowcast = YTD 2026 Jan-Sep / s; YTD = 19,096; s = YTD(y, Jan-Sep) / annual(y) for y in 2021-2025 (2021 0.595, 2022 0.656, 2023 0.707, 2024 0.737, 2025 0.757); low / middle / high use s = 0.757 / 0.707 / 0.595 = 25,228 / 26,998 / 32,110 units; the carried annual level is 30,376 units (the shipped rule's state level, mean of 2021-2025). Diagnostic only: no estimate uses it.

rows.label: Window sensitivity (disclosed, never subtracted)
rows.text: Five times the 2022–2025 mean: 129,985 homes against the shipped 151,882 (−21,897, −14.4%). Disclosed historical-window sensitivity. Named after the spike was seen, so not pre-registered. Not a replacement baseline; never subtracted from any reform or package result.

rows.text: Shipped rule on the state's own yearly totals: 151,882 homes; matches the baseline middle value 151,882.
